transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess the main thing that got me worried is my eating’s been kind of all over the place. It’s probably not a huge deal, but some days I realize I’ve basically skipped meals without meaning to, and then other nights I’m up late just going through takeout and snacks after midnight. It felt weird enough that I thought I should come in, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

I’m not totally sure about the number on the scale, honestly. I haven’t really been tracking it. But my appetite’s been weird, I guess—that’s more what scared me into coming in. Some days I’ll just forget to eat almost completely, and then other nights I’m up after midnight going through takeout and snacks. I know that probably sounds kind of messy, but… yeah, it’s been all over the place.
Do you find that your mood affects how much or how little you eat on any given day?

Yeah, I think so… at least it seems connected. Like when my mood is up or I’m kind of all over the place, I don’t really notice meals and I’ll just forget to eat. Then other nights, especially late, I’ll realize I’m just tearing through takeout or snacks after midnight. I don’t know if that’s the right way to explain it, but that’s the part that kind of scared me into coming in.
Do you ever feel guilty after eating, especially after those late-night snacks?

Um… yeah, I mean, not so much guilty about the food itself, I guess. It’s more like after I eat late, I start thinking about everything I’ve messed up.

Like I keep replaying mistakes I made with those Providence accounts at work, and then it turns into this whole thing where I’m thinking I blew my future and I’m useless, and probably everybody at work can see it. I know that might sound dramatic… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But yeah, that guilt kind of hits me.
Do you ever feel like you're eating an amount of food that's definitely more than most people would eat in a short period of time?

I mean… maybe? I don’t want to make it sound like it’s some huge thing, but there are nights where it feels like more than a normal snack, yeah. Like after midnight I’ll end up going through takeout and snacks, and afterward I’m kind of like, “Okay, that was probably a lot.”  

But it’s not every day. Other days I honestly forget meals completely, so it’s just been really all over the place.
Do you feel like you have control over what or how much you're eating during those late-night snacking episodes?

I guess… not as much as I’d like to say. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m totally out of control, because it’s not like that every night, but once I start after midnight, with takeout or snacks, I kind of just keep going and don’t really think about it until after.

Then other days it’s the opposite, like I’ll forget meals completely. So it’s just been really all over the place, honestly. That’s part of why it worried me enough to come in.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during those late-night snacking episodes?

Yeah… sometimes. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but on those nights after midnight, once I start with takeout or snacks, I can kind of tear through it before I really stop and think.

It’s weird because some days I forget meals completely, so it’s not like I’m eating like that all the time. It’s just been really all over the place, and honestly that’s part of what scared me enough to come in.
Do you ever try to make up for what you've eaten by doing something to counteract it, like exercising or vomiting?
No, not really. I mean… I might tell myself I’ll eat lighter the next day or something, but I don’t make myself throw up or go work out to “undo” it. Nothing like that. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like you're eating very quickly during those late-night snacking episodes?

Yeah… I think so, at least on those nights. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but when it’s after midnight and I get takeout or start on snacks, I kind of tear through it pretty fast before I’m really paying attention.

It’s not every day, though. Some days I honestly forget meals completely, so the whole eating thing has just been really all over the place. That’s what scared me enough to come in, if that makes sense.
Do you usually eat late at night when you're feeling stressed or anxious?

I’m not totally sure it’s always because I’m stressed or anxious, honestly. I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s more like… my eating has just been really inconsistent. Some days I’ll forget meals almost completely, and then other nights, after midnight, I’m tearing through takeout or snacks. That up-and-down part is what kind of scared me into coming in.
Do you feel guilty specifically about eating too much, rather than about other things in your life?

Not really about eating too much, no. I mean, I don’t feel great after those nights, but the guilt is more… other stuff.

Mostly work. I keep replaying mistakes I made with those Providence accounts, and I start thinking I blew my whole future over it. Like I’m just useless and everybody at work can see it. I know that probably sounds kind of dramatic, but that’s more what the guilt is about, if that answers it.
Do you usually eat more or less when you're feeling upset or emotional?

I guess it can go either way, if that makes sense. When I’m upset or just emotional, sometimes I don’t eat much at all and kind of forget meals. But then other nights, especially really late, I’ll end up going through takeout or snacks pretty fast.

I don’t know if that’s the “right” way to describe it, but it’s been all over the place enough that it worried me.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop yourself from continuing to eat once you've started eating during those late-night episodes?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m totally unable to stop, exactly… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But yeah, on those late nights, once I start with takeout or snacks, I can kind of just keep going without really thinking.

It’s more that my eating has been all over the place — some days I basically forget meals, and then after midnight I’m suddenly tearing through food. That swing is what scared me, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're eating without being able to control how much you're eating during those late-night snacking episodes?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely out of control or anything, but on those nights it kind of feels that way.

Honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is just that my eating has been all over the place. Some days I forget meals completely, and then other nights after midnight I’m tearing through takeout and snacks like I’m not really keeping track. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How often do these late-night eating episodes happen where you feel like you're eating a lot without being able to control it?

I’m not sure I’ve kept count exactly… I probably should have. It’s not, like, every single night, but it’s happened enough that it started to scare me.

Some days I’ll barely eat or forget meals, and then other nights after midnight I’m suddenly going through takeout or snacks way more than I meant to. So I don’t know the exact number, but it feels like a real pattern, if that makes sense.
How many times a week would you say you have one of these late-night eating episodes where you feel like you're eating a lot without being able to control it?

Maybe… a couple times a week? I’m sorry, I haven’t been tracking it exactly.

It’s not every night, but enough that I noticed it. Like I’ll have days where I basically forget to eat, and then other nights after midnight I’m going through takeout or snacks way more than I meant to. That’s the part that made me feel like something was off.
Do you feel like you're eating without being able to control how much you're eating during most of these late-night snacking episodes?

Yeah… most of the time when it happens, it does feel like I’m not really steering it the way I should be.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but honestly, that’s what scared me. My eating’s been kind of all over the place — some days I’ll forget meals completely, and then other nights after midnight I’m tearing through takeout and snacks before I even really think about it. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you usually feel guilty after these late-night eating episodes?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t love admitting that, but sometimes I do feel pretty bad about it afterward. Like I should’ve had it more together.

Honestly, the eating being so all over the place is what scared me into coming in — some days I forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout or snacks after midnight. Then afterward I’m kind of sitting there like, “Why did I do that?” If that makes sense.
Have you experienced significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to your eating habits?

I guess… yeah, it has caused some problems. I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart, because I’m still showing up and trying to handle things.

But my manager has started pulling me off some accounts because I’ve been making mistakes I normally wouldn’t. And HR got involved after I called the employee-assistance line, which was kind of embarrassing.

At home too, it just feels like things are slipping more than I want to admit. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

target_item.reason: The question is about the late-night eating episodes and appetite pattern, which are covered by the weight/appetite change symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I don’t love admitting that, but sometimes I do feel pretty bad about it afterward. Like I should’ve had it more together.

Honestly, the eating being so all over the place is what scared me into coming in — some days I forget meals completely, and then other nights I’m tearing through takeout or snacks after midnight. Then afterward I’m kind of sitting there like, “Why did I do that?” If that makes sense.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's eating pattern is consistent with Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder (OSFED)
doctor.question: Have you experienced significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to your eating habits?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My manager has started pulling me off accounts because I’m making mistakes I normally wouldn’t, and HR got involved after the employee-assistance call. I’m still showing up, but work and home both feel like they’re slipping out of my control.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms are causing significant distress or impairment in life areas, which is most directly covered by the functional impairment item.

patient.answer:
I guess… yeah, it has caused some problems. I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart, because I’m still showing up and trying to handle things.

But my manager has started pulling me off some accounts because I’ve been making mistakes I normally wouldn’t. And HR got involved after I called the employee-assistance line, which was kind of embarrassing.

At home too, it just feels like things are slipping more than I want to admit. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of recurrent episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period, lack of control over eating during these episodes, and significant distress or impairment in social or occupational areas of life meet the diagnostic criteria for Other eating disorders, specifically indicative of a condition like binge eating disorder or a similar disorder not otherwise specified.
